requirements: Repair /app/pipeline.py to mosaic two synthetic GeoTIFFs. Accept
--input DIRECTORY --output DIRECTORY. Input contains reference.tif (target grid,
EPSG:4326) and secondary.tif (different grid, EPSG:3857). Each has a single float32
band and NoData=-9999. Reproject secondary onto the EXACT reference CRS, affine,
width and height using nearest-neighbor sampling at target pixel centers. A
target center outside the source extent is missing. Never treat NoData as zero.
For each pixel, average the two valid values when both exist, retain a sole valid
value, and emit -9999 if neither exists. Save float32 output/mosaic.tif with exact
target georeferencing and NoData metadata. Also write output/summary.json with
exactly valid_count (integer) and mean (number or null for no valid cells).
Pixel and mean tolerance: 1e-5 absolute. Repeat execution must be idempotent.
Use NumPy/rasterio already installed. Public input directory: /app/input.
Run the program there and leave repaired /app/pipeline.py. Hidden tests use
different raster values/NoData under the same contract. These are generated
synthetic fixtures, not satellite observations or a real geospatial dataset.

requirements: Repair /app/pipeline.py, a broken interval normalization utility.
Accept --input JSON --output DIRECTORY. JSON input is an array of [start,end]
integer pairs, each describing a half-open interval [start,end). Discard empty
intervals (start == end). If ANY pair is reversed (start > end), emit exactly
{"error":"reversed_interval"}; do not silently swap its endpoints.
Otherwise emit {"intervals":[[start,end],...],"covered":N} in output/result.json,
where intervals are the sorted disjoint union; touching intervals MUST merge,
duplicates collapse, negative coordinates are allowed, and covered is total
integer length (sum of end-start). Empty input yields intervals=[] and covered=0.
The importable function merge_intervals(intervals) must return that same object
without modifying the input. CLI must overwrite outputs idempotently.
Use Python standard library. Input fixture: /app/input/intervals.json. Run the
program and leave repaired /app/pipeline.py. Hidden tests use other valid JSONs
under this contract. All fixture data is synthetic.

requirements: Repair /app/pipeline.py. It must accept --input CSV --output DIRECTORY,
read the CSV, and emit summary.json as a JSON array sorted by station_id. Each row
has exactly station_id (string), count (integer), mean_c (number). The input has
station_id,timestamp,value,unit,status,revision; irrelevant columns may occur.
Timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 strings ending Z. For duplicate (station_id,timestamp),
select the row with largest integer revision BEFORE checking status/value. If that
selected row is invalid, discard that timestamp; do not resurrect an older value.
Revisions per duplicate key are unique. A row is valid only when status is exactly
'ok' and value is a finite number. Blank status is unknown and must be discarded.
Units are C (Celsius), F (convert (value-32)*5/9), and K (value-273.15).
Aggregate valid readings by station after conversion; omit stations with none.
Round mean_c to six decimals using round-to-even; numeric tolerance is 1e-6.
Overwrite output deterministically on repeated calls; input order must not matter.
Use Python standard library only. Input is /app/input/observations.csv. Run the
program on it and leave repaired source /app/pipeline.py. Hidden tests use other
CSVs under exactly this contract. Synthetic fixtures, no real sensor observations.
